omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Exactly 1; missing requires legacy migration preview.
description: The version of the configuration file format. Keep this at 1 so the app can read the file. This is not a financial assumption.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: The first calendar year of retirement. Ages are calculated as this year minus each person’s birth year. Starting balances and today’s spending amounts apply at the beginning of this year.

constraints: 1...100000 inclusive; exact; memory preflight may reject.
description: How many possible retirement futures to simulate. More paths give steadier estimates of probabilities and percentiles, but take more time and memory. Each path uses the same financial rules with different market and medical outcomes.

The number that controls the random draws. Reusing the same seed, configuration and reference data reproduces the same paths. Use an integer from 0 through 4,294,967,295; the adjacent button chooses one randomly.

constraints: At least the younger start age (or the single start age); everyone stays alive through that max_age year; memory preflight bounds horizon.
description: The simulation includes the year when the younger person reaches this age. Both people are assumed to remain alive throughout. A path ends earlier if its net assets, including property equity after mortgages, reach zero or become negative.

constraints: Within active history; window >=10 years.
description: The earliest historical year that can be sampled for US investment returns, US inflation and US home prices. All series use the same selected years to preserve their historical relationships. Choose a window containing at least 10 complete years.

constraints: Within active history; >=sample_start+9.
description: The latest historical year that can be sampled. Together with Sample start, this sets the pool of past outcomes; it does not set the final retirement year or predict future returns.

The average length of consecutive historical years kept together before the simulation jumps to another historical starting point. Longer blocks preserve more of the sequences seen during booms and crises. This is an average, rather than a fixed block length.

constraints: -0.1...0.1; added to sampled US stock/bond returns.
description: A yearly shift added to sampled US stock and bond returns, expressing a view that markets will run hotter or cooler than history. Zero replays history unchanged. Enter a decimal: 0.02 adds two percentage points a year. Volatility, crash sequences, inflation and cash returns are unchanged.

constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: The long-run annual home-economy inflation assumption. Home-domicile spending follows the resulting home price index. Enter a decimal: 0.04 means 4% a year. Ignored when the domicile is the US, whose inflation replays history.

constraints: -0.5...0.5 under the v1 spec rate range.
description: How much last year’s home-economy inflation carries into the next year, relative to the long-run mean. Zero removes that persistence; a positive value makes high or low inflation more likely to continue. This is a persistence factor, not an inflation rate.

constraints: 0...0.5; generated CPI must exceed -1.
description: The size of the random annual changes in home-economy inflation. Zero removes these random changes; 0.018 means a standard deviation of 1.8 percentage points. The long-run mean and persistence still apply.

constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: The home-economy inflation rate immediately before the first simulated year. It feeds the first year’s inflation calculation through the persistence setting. Enter a decimal: 0.04 means 4%.

The starting exchange rate in CNY per US dollar. For example, 6.69 means one dollar buys 6.69 yuan before conversion costs. A lower number makes CNY spending more expensive in dollars. Refresh market data updates this to the latest available observation.

The starting reference exchange rate used by purchasing-power parity (PPP) mode. This reference moves with the difference between China and US inflation, plus the real trend setting. It is a modeling assumption and may differ from the current spot rate. Drift mode does not use it to move the exchange rate.
In PPP mode, how quickly the exchange rate moves toward the inflation-adjusted reference rate. Zero removes this pull; higher values make the adjustment faster. Drift mode ignores this setting.

The size of random annual exchange-rate moves, measured on a logarithmic scale. Zero removes exchange-rate noise. A value of 0.042 is approximately 4.2% annual volatility for small moves; it is not a guaranteed annual change.

constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: An annual trend in the PPP reference rate beyond the China–US inflation difference. A positive value raises CNY per dollar, making the yuan weaker; a negative value makes it stronger. This is a logarithmic change: 0.01 is about 1% a year. Drift mode ignores it.

constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: PPP moves the exchange rate toward a reference that follows the China–US inflation difference. Drift instead applies the chosen annual drift. Both modes add the exchange-rate noise specified by FX sigma.

constraints: -0.2...0.2; annual LOG change, not simple percentage.
description: The annual change in CNY per dollar used only in Drift mode, before random noise. Positive values weaken the yuan; negative values strengthen it. This is a logarithmic change: 0.01 means about a 1.005% increase a year. PPP mode ignores this setting.

constraints: 0 <= spread <1; conversion denominators strictly positive.
description: The cost of exchanging USD and CNY in either direction. Enter a decimal: 0.003 means 0.3%. Higher costs require more dollars to fund the same CNY spending and reduce dollars received when exchanging CNY.

constraints: Nonnegative nominal USD; not indexed.
description: The annual USD-to-CNY conversion amount per person used to flag a possible quota issue. For two people the model compares against twice this amount. It marks the ledger when exceeded; it does not block a conversion or model bank approval. This amount is not increased with inflation.

constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: Extra annual medical price inflation added to China inflation. For example, China inflation of 4% plus 0.02 here gives 6% medical price growth that year. It affects the base medical budget, medical shocks and late-life care; age-related growth is a separate setting.

constraints: 0...1; NYU 2025 dividends / beginning-year S&P level = 0.01336; splits total return, does not add return.
description: The annual share of a brokerage stock holding treated as reinvested dividends for tax calculations. The rest of the sampled total return is price movement; this yield does not add to the total return. Refresh uses the latest complete NYU year’s dividends divided by the beginning-of-year S&P 500 level. Enter a decimal: 0.013 means 1.3%.

constraints: 0...1; FRED DGS10 2026-10-15 = 0.051; par Treasury income proxy, not portfolio coupon or extra return.
description: The annual share of a brokerage bond holding treated as reinvested coupon income for tax calculations. This income is already part of the sampled total return and is not added again. Refresh uses the latest FRED 10-year Treasury par yield as an income proxy, which may differ from your holdings’ actual coupons. Enter a decimal: 0.051 means 5.1%.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: One domicile country for the whole household; drives China-tax routing for every member.
description: The household’s domicile for income-tax purposes: US or China. One country covers one or two people. China domicile brings modeled foreign investment and pension income into China tax from the first year. US domicile follows the configured six-year reset assumption for when China tax begins.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Start age 18...100; actual 1986 annualized placeholder.
description: Person A’s birth year. Age is calculated by calendar year rather than exact birthday. It determines retirement-account access, medical-shock probability, benefit timing and which person sets the Max age endpoint.

omission: retired from the UI; accepted when present but no effect on calculations
constraints: M=male, F=female; lifespan uses the same fixed horizon for the household.
description: Person A’s descriptive sex. Everyone remains alive to the same planning endpoint, so this choice does not change lifespan, medical probabilities or financial calculations.

omission: unchecked means non-citizen; explicit answer not required
constraints: Citizens are US tax residents; non-citizens use NRA branch.
description: Whether person A is a US citizen. Citizenship is checked against the chosen US income-tax status. A citizen must use Resident treatment; a noncitizen must explicitly resolve their tax-residency status.

omission: derived from us_citizen when omitted; explicit contradictions still block Run
constraints: Citizen/resident or noncitizen/nonresident supported; resident alien cannot use NRA.
description: The US income-tax treatment for person A. Resident applies the model’s US resident income and investment tax rules; Nonresident uses its supported nonresident categories. Unresolved blocks a run. Citizenship alone does not establish a noncitizen’s income-tax residency.

constraints: Annual pension or annuity payout in today’s USD; 0 means none.
description: Person A’s yearly pension or annuity payout in today’s USD, received as spendable cash once payments start. It is taxed as ordinary US income and never taxed by China in this model. Enter 0 for no pension.

constraints: First payout year is the year this age is reached; 0...120.
description: The age at which person A’s pension or annuity starts paying; the first payout arrives in the year that age is reached. Payments continue every year through the planning horizon.

constraints: On follows US CPI; off pays the same nominal dollars yearly.
description: Whether person A’s pension or annuity rises with US inflation each year. On tracks the cost of living; off pays the same nominal dollars every year.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Start age 18...100; actual 1986 annualized placeholder.
description: Person B’s birth year. Age is calculated by calendar year rather than exact birthday. It determines retirement-account access, medical-shock probability, benefit timing and which person sets the Max age endpoint.

omission: retired from the UI; accepted when present but no effect on calculations
constraints: M=male, F=female; lifespan uses the same fixed horizon for the household.
description: Person B’s descriptive sex. Everyone remains alive to the same planning endpoint, so this choice does not change lifespan, medical probabilities or financial calculations.

omission: unchecked means non-citizen; explicit answer not required
constraints: Citizens are US tax residents; non-citizens use NRA branch.
description: Whether person B is a US citizen. Citizenship is checked against the chosen US income-tax status. A citizen must use Resident treatment; a noncitizen must explicitly resolve their tax-residency status.

omission: derived from us_citizen when omitted; explicit contradictions still block Run
constraints: Citizen/resident or noncitizen/nonresident supported; resident alien cannot use NRA.
description: The US income-tax treatment for person B. Resident applies the model’s US resident income and investment tax rules; Nonresident uses its supported nonresident categories. Unresolved blocks a run. Citizenship alone does not establish a noncitizen’s income-tax residency.

constraints: Annual pension or annuity payout in today’s USD; 0 means none.
description: Person B’s yearly pension or annuity payout in today’s USD, received as spendable cash once payments start. It is taxed as ordinary US income and never taxed by China in this model. Enter 0 for no pension.

constraints: First payout year is the year this age is reached; 0...120.
description: The age at which person B’s pension or annuity starts paying; the first payout arrives in the year that age is reached. Payments continue every year through the planning horizon.

constraints: On follows US CPI; off pays the same nominal dollars yearly.
description: Whether person B’s pension or annuity rises with US inflation each year. On tracks the cost of living; off pays the same nominal dollars every year.

constraints: Nonnegative money; valid growth factors.
description: Annual growth in the base medical budget due to aging, on top of medical price inflation. Enter a decimal: 0.04 means another 4% per elapsed year. This affects the recurring medical base; shocks have their own age-based probability and care has its own growth setting.

constraints: Nonnegative money; valid growth factors.
description: Allow random large medical expenses for each person in addition to the recurring medical base. Turning this off removes those shocks while keeping the base medical budget and enabled late-life care.

Each person’s annual chance of a medical shock at age 60. Enter a decimal: 0.02 means a 2% chance per year per person. The doubling-years setting adjusts this chance for younger and older ages, with a maximum of 100%.

How many additional years of age double a person’s annual medical-shock probability. For example, 8 makes the chance at age 68 twice the chance at age 60. The probability is lower at younger ages and capped at 100%.

constraints: Nonnegative money; valid growth factors.
description: The medical shock size in today’s household currency, before medical price inflation. Every shock costs this inflation-adjusted amount.

constraints: Always additional medical expense; starts at selected age and continues through the planning horizon; monthly>=0; real growth in[-.5,.5]; follows medical price index.
description: Include the configured monthly care expense once the earliest-born person reaches the care start age. Care is always an additional medical expense and continues through the last simulated year. It is separate from the included medical base and random shocks.

constraints: Always additional medical expense; starts at selected age and continues through the planning horizon; monthly>=0; real growth in[-.5,.5]; follows medical price index.
description: The age at which the household’s monthly care expense begins, including that year, measured on the earliest-born person. Care continues to the simulation’s final year; there is no separate end age.

constraints: Always additional medical expense; starts at selected age and continues through the planning horizon; monthly>=0; real growth in[-.5,.5]; follows medical price index.
description: The household’s monthly care cost in today’s CNY. The simulation charges 12 months each active year and adjusts the amount for medical price inflation and care real growth. It is always additional to the base annual budget.

constraints: Always additional medical expense; starts at selected age and continues through the planning horizon; monthly>=0; real growth in[-.5,.5]; follows medical price index.
description: Annual growth in the care amount beyond medical price inflation. Enter a decimal: 0.01 means another 1% per year. Growth is measured from the simulation start, including years before care begins, so the eventual care amount remains expressed in today’s prices at entry.

constraints: >=0; total base annual household-currency budget. Ordinary spending is annual minus included_health, indexed by the domicile price index.
description: The household’s total base annual budget in today’s CNY, including the medical amount entered below. Ordinary spending is this amount minus Included health CNY. Medical is counted once. Optional medical shocks, care, one-time expenses and income taxes can require additional money.

constraints: >=0; single annual base medical budget for the household; included in annual once, before optional shocks/care.
description: The combined annual base medical budget for both people in today’s CNY. It is already included in Annual CNY, so it is not added to that budget again. This part grows with medical price inflation and aging; the rest of the budget grows with China inflation.

constraints: On lets the non-medical budget flex with portfolio years.
description: Lets the non-medical budget flex with portfolio years. After an up year spending can rise up to the raise limit; after a down year it can fall to the cut limit. Medical spending, shocks, care and one-time costs never flex.

constraints: 0...1; max non-medical spend cut after a down year.
description: The largest fraction the non-medical budget can fall after a down year, as a decimal: 0.15 means spending can drop to 85% of plan. Each down year draws a random cut between none and this limit.

constraints: 0...1; max non-medical spend raise after an up year.
description: The largest fraction the non-medical budget can rise after an up year, as a decimal: 0.15 means spending can rise to 115% of plan. Each up year draws a random raise between none and this limit.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: A label for this one-time expense, such as relocation or a car purchase. The label helps you identify it and does not change the calculation.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: The calendar year when this expense is paid, once. The expense is paid only if the simulation path reaches that year.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: The one-time expense in today’s prices, using the currency selected here. It grows with China inflation for CNY expenses or US inflation for USD expenses until the payment year.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: The currency of the entered amount. CNY expenses follow China inflation; USD expenses follow US inflation and use that year’s exchange rate when reported in CNY. New costs default to the domicile currency.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Fixed identifier: brokerage, after_tax or pre_tax; all three accounts required in that order.
description: The fixed identifier for this account: brokerage for Non-retirement liquid assets, after_tax for After-tax retirement savings, or pre_tax for Pre-tax retirement savings. Withdrawal order and property-sale destinations use this identifier. Surplus cash always goes to Non-retirement liquid assets.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Fixed per position: brokerage, then after_tax, then pre_tax; matches name.
description: The fixed account type, matching its identifier. Brokerage is a USD account with taxes on investment income and realized gains. Pre-tax is a pre-tax retirement account with withdrawal taxes and access rules. After-tax withdrawals are US tax free, but the chosen China pension treatment still applies. Both retirement accounts have age-based access.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Strict known key; finite numbers; integers must be safe integers; see spec §9.2.
description: The account’s starting market value in USD. This is the full balance before future withdrawal taxes. It is divided among the selected asset allocations. A brokerage account’s tax cost basis always equals this balance. With two people the balance is owned evenly; with one person that person owns it fully.

omission: optional asset key=0; allocation required for all three accounts
constraints: >=0; subset of three keys; sum=1 +/-1e-6.
description: The fraction of this brokerage or retirement account invested in US stocks. Enter 0.60 for 60%, not 60. The three allocation fractions must add to 1. This sets starting balances, new deposits and annual rebalancing targets. Income treatment is fixed by asset: stocks pay qualified dividends, bonds pay coupon interest with zero-gain sales, and cash earns money-market interest.

omission: optional asset key=0; allocation required for all three accounts
constraints: >=0; subset of three keys; sum=1 +/-1e-6.
description: The fraction of this brokerage or retirement account invested in US bonds. Enter 0.60 for 60%, not 60. The three allocation fractions must add to 1. This sets starting balances, new deposits and annual rebalancing targets. Income treatment is fixed by asset: stocks pay qualified dividends, bonds pay coupon interest with zero-gain sales, and cash earns money-market interest.

omission: optional asset key=0; allocation required for all three accounts
constraints: >=0; subset of three keys; sum=1 +/-1e-6.
description: The fraction of this brokerage or retirement account invested in USD cash. Enter 0.60 for 60%, not 60. The three allocation fractions must add to 1. This sets starting balances, new deposits and annual rebalancing targets. Income treatment is fixed by asset: stocks pay qualified dividends, bonds pay coupon interest with zero-gain sales, and cash earns money-market interest.

omission: optional pre-tax only; forbidden for other types
constraints: Declared qualifying condition; verify exception and penalty treatment.
description: Declare that this pre-tax retirement account qualifies for the model’s Rule of 55 exception. It permits access from age 55 without the early-withdrawal penalty. Ordinary withdrawal income tax still applies. This is not a general exception for every IRA or former employer account.

omission: optional pre-tax only; forbidden for other types
constraints: Declared early access; verify exception and penalty treatment.
description: Allow withdrawals from this pre-tax retirement account before the model’s normal access age of 60. Such withdrawals can incur ordinary income tax and the early-withdrawal penalty unless the configured Rule of 55 exception applies. This does not unlock early after-tax withdrawals.

constraints: Omission uses the declared default; unchecking disables last-resort sales.
description: Allow the model to attempt a property sale when account withdrawals cannot meet a cash need, including properties otherwise marked Hold. Turning this off keeps property from being sold solely to cover a shortage. A sale may fail if closing costs, the mortgage and withholding require unaffordable extra cash.

omission: optional; omit to leave the property unnamed
constraints: Free text for display only; never affects the simulation.
description: An optional reminder name for this property, such as its address. It is only shown in the editor and never affects the simulation.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: Unique persisted nonempty ID; US real property only, citizen treatment for all owners.
description: A unique, persistent identifier for this US property. All owners use citizen tax treatment; there is no foreign-owner withholding.

omission: derived from household size when omitted (1 solo, 0.5 joint); hidden from the Builder
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Person A’s ownership share of the property; the rest belongs to B. Enter 0.5 for equal ownership. This splits rent, basis and gains between the two taxpayers.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: The property’s starting market value in USD before subtracting the mortgage. Property equity is market value minus the outstanding loan. Held property follows sampled US home returns with no premium or individual price noise.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: The property’s total original USD tax basis before subtracting depreciation already taken. It is split by ownership share. Together with depreciation and sale costs, it determines the US taxable gain or loss on sale.

constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: The fraction of the property’s tax basis assigned to land, which is not depreciated. Enter 0.20 for 20% land and 80% building. Only the building portion is eligible for the model’s annual rental depreciation.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Total USD depreciation already claimed before the simulation starts. It reduces the adjusted US tax basis and remaining building depreciation. On sale it can put part of a gain into the special depreciation-related tax category.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: The starting outstanding mortgage principal in USD. It reduces property equity. The mortgage payment reduces available rental cash, and any remaining balance must be repaid at sale.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: The fixed annual mortgage interest rate. Enter a decimal: 0.04 means 4%. It is used with the loan balance and years left to calculate annual payments, interest and principal repayment.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: The remaining mortgage term in years. Together with the starting balance and interest rate, it sets the annual amortizing payment. A positive mortgage balance requires a positive remaining term.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Monthly gross rent in today’s USD before expenses; full occupancy is assumed. The model annualizes it, applies US inflation and rent real growth, then subtracts operating costs and mortgage payments.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Annual maintenance cost in today’s USD, covering management and upkeep in one figure. It grows with US inflation and is deducted from rental cash flow and the rental-income calculation.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: The starting annual property-tax bill in USD. Future bills follow modeled property-price changes. This is an operating expense separate from tax on rental income or a sale.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Annual property insurance in today’s USD. It grows with US inflation and is deducted as a rental operating expense. This is property insurance, separate from the household medical budget.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Monthly homeowners-association fees in today’s USD. The model charges 12 months each year, increases them with US inflation and deducts them from rental cash flow.

constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Annual rent growth beyond US inflation. Enter 0 for rent that only follows inflation, or 0.01 for another 1% per year. Negative values model rent lagging behind inflation.

constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Sale costs as a fraction of the property’s gross sale price. Enter 0.06 for 6%. These costs reduce closing cash and the net price used to calculate the sale gain; mortgage repayment is separate.

omission: required; blank stays omitted and blocks Run
constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: Hold keeps the property unless last-resort sales are enabled and cash is needed. Sell year attempts a sale in the specified calendar year. A path that ends earlier cannot make a later sale.

constraints: See spec §§5.8/9.2; money>=0, valid factors, fractions in[0,1].
description: The first calendar year to attempt selling this property when its strategy is Sell year. If a sale cannot close, the model can try again in later years while the property is held. Other strategies ignore this setting, and a path that has ended cannot make a sale.
